messages.subject: Re: desktop nblast: missing registrations
messages.body_plain:
Dear Christa,

Thanks for your interest in the nblast and related tools (the natverse).

1. The install instructions you need are here

https://github.com/natverse/nat.flybrains#installation

In particular you need to do:

   nat.flybrains::download_jefferislab_registrations()

in order to download the additional bridging registrations that you need
that will connect FCWB (FlyCircuit) to FAFB (EM) via JFRC2013 (Janelia
confocal template).

You should end ups with something like the attached.

2. You will likely be able to install RcppArmadillo using the binary
version from CRAN.

> install.packages('RcppArmadillo')

   There is a binary version available but the source version is later:
                    binary      source needs_compilation
RcppArmadillo 0.9.800.4.0 0.9.850.1.0              TRUE

Do you want to install from sources the package which needs compilation?
(Yes/no/cancel)

  Answer no and you should be ok.

Best of luck and let us know how things work,

Greg.

PS I have taken the liberty of ccing the nat-user mailing list since
others may find this answer helpful.

messages.subject: neuPrint Janelia hemibrain skeleton -> NBLAST
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I would like to use NBLAST to search for GAL4 lines using a skeleton of a neuron that I downloaded from neuprint.janelia.org <http://neuprint.janelia.org> but I'm not sure how to prepare my input for NBLAST. I thought the hemibrain EM data had been registered to the JRC2018 template brain and that I might be able to use the Saalfeld Lab registrations to do something like what I pasted below, but when I plot my untransformed neuron and the JRC2018F template brain they are not aligned so I must be misunderstanding the necessary steps! I would appreciate any advice you might have on what additional bridging registrations or formatting is required before running NBLAST on hemibrain skeletons. Thank you so much!!

n = read.neuron("file.swc")
n_trans = xform_brain(my_neuron, sample=JRC2018F, reference=FCWB)
n.dps = dotprops(my_neuron_transf)
## then run nblast on n.dps

messages.subject: Re: neuPrint Janelia hemibrain skeleton -> NBLAST
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm not a core nat contributor but I made the JRC2018 template, and the Saalfeld Lab registrations you referred to.

Just one misunderstanding - the "raw" hemibrain dataset is not aligned to any standard template.  It's in its own "space."

I'm about to release a transformation that will take neurons from the hemibrain space to the JRC2018F,
and once that's ready you'll be able to do what you'd like.  It will be soon.

John

P.S.  It's been slow to release this transform, because some biologists here at Janelia were unsatisfied with a
preliminary registration we had, and we've been spending the last week tuning and evaluating it. We don't want
to release a sub-standard "product".  Thanks for your patience.

messages.body_plain:
Dear John, Thanks for responding to this!

Dear Abby, As John explains you need a transformation to take you from the raw hemibrain dataset to JRC2018F and he is the one who generated that. We have been using a pre-release version of the transform for some time now for the purposes that you describe. The natverse has infrastructure in place to make use of the final transform when he is able to make publicly available.

The likelihood is that you will use the package

https://github.com/natverse/nat.jrcbrains

Once you have this installed and the relevant registrations installed

library(nat.jrcbrains)
download_saalfeldlab_registrations()

This already lets you use John's registrations for light level data. You will soon be able to do something like:

> > n_trans = xform_brain(my_neuron, sample=JRC2018FIBF, reference=FCWB)
> > n.dps = dotprops(my_neuron_transf)

But once again John is the one providing the key missing ingredient here!

All the best,

Greg.

messages.subject: Comparing 2 SWC files
messages.body_plain:
Is there a way in R to use NBLAST to take two SWC files and compare them for similarity (possibly outputing some sort of similarity score)?

Thanks for your help,
Corey Elowsky

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Comparing 2 SWC files
messages.body_plain:
Dear Corey,

This a pretty standard operation at this point. See docs for read.neurons to bring in the SWC files, dotprops to convert them into the format used by nblast or nblast_allbyall

See https://github.com/natverse/nat.examples <https://github.com/natverse/nat.examples?files=1> and

https://github.com/natverse/nat.nblast

For more information.

The main issue is the spatial scale of your neurons. NBLAST v2 is tuned for drosophila neurons. You either need to rescale your neurons to match or choose a different scoring procedure.

Best,

Greg.

Sent from my iPhone
